summary: The Tavascan is Cupra's only battery-electric model in Australia now that the Born has been withdrawn, and it is a coupe-roofed mid-size SUV built on the same MEB platform as the Volkswagen ID.5 and Skoda Enyaq. Australian reviewers consistently rate the chassis above its rivals — Chasing Cars and CarsGuide both single out the steering and body control as sharper than a Tesla Model Y or BYD Sealion 7 — while criticising the haptic controls, the 135kW DC charging peak and the complete absence of connected services. Buyers should note this two-grade range is in run-out: Cupra announced an updated line-up on 30 June 2026, arriving from late August, which adds a cheaper entry grade and repositions the VZ above the $75,000 FBT cap.
pros: Reviewers rate the chassis the best in the segment: Chasing Cars called the Endurance's chassis 'agile and adjustable' with crisp steering, and CarsGuide judged the ride a genuine step above the Tesla Model Y and BYD Sealion 7 it is priced against

Both grades sit under the $75,000 FBT-exemption cap for novated leases, the VZ by just $510 — and the replacement VZ announced for late August 2026 is priced at $75,490, which forfeits that concession, so the run-out car is materially cheaper to salary-package
540 litres seats-up and 1,550 litres seats-down with a power tailgate and kick sensor, and a completely flat rear floor that makes the middle seat genuinely usable for an adult

Five-year unlimited-kilometre warranty is factory-backed and unconditional — it is not tied to servicing inside the Cupra network — with the high-voltage battery separately covered for 8 years/160,000km including a 70 per cent capacity floor
The 250kW VZ runs 0-100km/h in 5.5 seconds and adds DCC adaptive dampers, a fixed panoramic roof and matrix high beam over the 210kW Endurance, none of which the base car can be optioned with
cons: This range is superseded from late August 2026 by an updated line-up with a 10.25-inch driver display, physical steering wheel buttons and a $55,490 entry grade — the run-out car means older cabin tech and an immediate resale hit
135kW DC peak is slow for 2026: a Kia EV5 or Zeekr 7X at similar money refills faster, and Chasing Cars called the 28-minute 10-80 per cent claim disappointing for a 77kWh pack
No vehicle-to-load, no head-up display and no connected services at all — no smartphone app, no remote preconditioning and no over-the-air updates, features that cars $15,000 cheaper now include

Cupra is a marginal brand here — just 257 Tavascans delivered in Australia to the end of May 2026, the same as the Skoda Elroq it shares a platform with — so parts, specialist repairers and resale all carry small-volume risk
Chasing Cars measured 18.3kWh/100km in the real world for about 421km against the 531km WLTP claim, and criticised the grainy handover between regenerative braking and the rear drum brakes
